subject: N mixture point count abundance averages

messages.author: 40c39176b13a80bb
messages.subject: N mixture point count abundance averages
parts:
A question motivated by the example of computing avg.abundance on p.
32 of the unmarked package manual. I am analyzing point count data
(100 survey sites) with the pcount function and have various potential
mean-centered site covariates on the lambda (abundance) side. When
there are no covariates, I of course obtain the same average whether I
use 'backTransform(linearCom . . . or mean(predict(. . . as in the
example below. As I add covariates, the results progressively
diverge. The average abundance computed by mean(predict . . .
corresponds with the average lambda presented, say, by the Presence
program, but the logic of using the backTransform(linearComb . . .
function appeals also, as long as the covariatesare mean-centered.
Am I misapplying or misunderstanding one or the other approach? Which
average is most appropriate to present?

Thanks in advance, and many thanks for the unmarked package!

M0<-pcount(~1 ~1,data1)
B0a<-backTransform(linearComb(M0,coefficients=c(1),type="state"))
#B0a estimate=0.242 SE=0.052
B0b<-mean(predict(M0,type="state"))
#B0b estimate=0.242 SE=0.052

M1<-pcount(~1 ~scale(lat),data1)
B1a<-backTransform(linearComb(M1,coefficients=c(1,0),type="state"))
#B1a estimate=0.234 SE=0.052
B1b<-mean(predict(M1,type="state"))
#B1b estimate=0.245 SE=0.069

M2<-pcount(~1 ~scale(lat)+scale(lon),data1)
B2a <-
backTransform(linearComb(M2,coefficients=c(1,0,0),type="state"))
#B2a estimate=0.184 SE=0.051
B2b <- mean(predict(M2,type="state"))
#B2b estimate=0.249 SE=0.085


M3<-pcount(~1 ~scale(lat)+scale(lon)+scale(marifh),data1)
B3a <-
backTransform(linearComb(M3,coefficients=c(1,0,0,0),type="state"))
#B3a estimate=0.160 SE=0.049
B3b <- mean(predict(M3,type="state"))
#B3b estimate=0.262 SE=0.103

M4<-pcount(~1 ~scale(lat)+scale(lon)+scale(marifh)
+scale(agric),data1)
B4a <-
backTransform(linearComb(M4,coefficients=c(1,0,0,0,0),type="state"))
#B4a estimate=0.125 SE=0.045
B4b <- mean(predict(M4,type="state"))
#B4b estimate=0.274 SE=0.120

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] N mixture point count abundance averages
parts:
Hi Richard,

I think that the answer to your question depends upon what quantity
you are interested in. In your first approach, where you use
backTransform and linearComb, you are getting the expected abundance
when you covariates have values of 0. In your second approach you are
taking the average of expected abundance for the observed covariate
values in your dataset. These are different, as the results indicate.
An alternative would be to provide an estimate of population size
using:

sum(predict(M4,type="state")$Predicted)

You could get SE and CI using the delta method or by bootstrapping.
See ?parboot for an example of the latter.

If you are interested in plotting relationships between abundance and
covariates, you could create a new data.frame with the covariate
values of interest, and then use predict. See the example on page 5
of:

vignette("unmarked")


Glad you like the package.

Richard
